text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam's government has expressed optimism about developments in various fields this year saying positive results have been recorded in many areas, especially external relations.
-- Vietnam's leaders have sent greetings to their Chinese counterparts to mark China's 47th National Day.
-- The Asian Development Bank will give $1.03 million towards improving transportation on northern Vietnam's Red River.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi told Laotian General Political Commissar Khanphuong Chanthaphomma during a meeting on Monday he welcomes regular exchanges between the two armies.

-- The State Bank of Vietnam has lowered the ceiling on short-term interest rates to 1.25 percent per month and medium and long-term rates to 1.35 percent. The new ceiling rates are effective from October 1. - - - -

-- The Chairman of the Government Office, Le Xuan Trinh, told a news conference on Monday the country is facing big difficulties with budget receipts. He said imports of cement and consumer goods should be reduced in the last three months of 1996.
-- Vietnam's Chief of Staff Lieutenant-General Pham Van Tra and his Laotian counterpart Duongchay Phichit have agreed to consolidate and strengthen bilateral relations.
-- The fourth Vietnam-Japan Economic Joint conference was held in Hanoi on Monday to help boost bilateral trade and Japanese investment in Vietnam.

-- Twenty-six foreign investment projects with total capital of $400 million have been licensed in Hanoi so far this year. Delays and changes in the construction licensing process are among the main obtacles facing foreign investors in Hanoi. - - - -
